writing.exampleCaption: Bounded, with a policy for what leaves and when.
writing.explanation: A TTL trades staleness for simplicity, explicit invalidation trades simplicity for correctness, and write-through trades write latency for both. The failure modes are the interesting part: a stampede when a hot key expires, and unbounded growth without an eviction policy. Naming which staleness your product can tolerate is the real answer.
writing.feedback: A single flight lock or early refresh is what stops the herd.
